prompt.context: You are working for the manager of Real Madrid. The manager of Manchester United is calling your client and offers to sell Wayne Rooney. Real Madrid is a professional soccer team based in Madrid. Manchester United is a professional soccer team based in London. Wayne Rooney is an English soccer player, widely considered the best English player; he plays forward. In soccer, clubs generally pay a transfer fee to get players out of existing contracts.
prompt.question: How much would you advise Real Madrid to bid for Wayne Rooney?

clarifying_info.q: Who is Real Madrid's president and what is his financial position?
clarifying_info.a: Real Madrid's president is absurdly rich. If he is convinced that Wayne Rooney is worth it, he will be willing to pay any price.

clarifying_info.q: Is Manchester United motivated to sell and at what floor?
clarifying_info.a: Manchester United's jersey sponsor is AIG. Rumors have it that they might be in need of cash. However, they are not willing to sell Wayne Rooney below fair value.

clarifying_info.q: Are there other clubs interested in Wayne Rooney?
clarifying_info.a: Candidate may assume several clubs to be interested in Wayne Rooney.

clarifying_info.q: Are there other forwards on the market?
clarifying_info.a: There are other forwards on the market while several clubs are interested in Wayne Rooney.

clarifying_info.q: Is the soccer player market homogeneous across Europe?
clarifying_info.a: Candidate may assume a homogeneous market across Europe.

clarifying_info.q: What contract length should we assume?
clarifying_info.a: Assume a 5-year contract for Wayne Rooney. The existing contracts of comparable players were similar in length and pay.

clarifying_info.q: Were the comparable transfer fees fairly priced?
clarifying_info.a: Candidate may assume that the prices for comparable players represent fair market value.

exhibits.title: Transfer fees for comparable players
exhibits.shows: A table of recent high-profile soccer player transfers showing the player name, transfer year, new team, old team, and transfer price in euros.
exhibits.data: Kaka: 2009, Real Madrid from AC Milan, 65M Euro; Andrej Schewtschenko: 2006, Chelsea London from AC Milan, 46M Euro; Ronaldo: 2002, Real Madrid from Inter Milan, 45M Euro

exhibits.title: Revenue streams and value-based pricing inputs
exhibits.shows: A breakdown of Real Madrid's main revenue streams and the expected incremental profit impact of adding Wayne Rooney in each area.
exhibits.data: Ticket Sales: stadium already sold out, no incremental impact; Jersey Sales: 100M fans, 3% buy Rooney jersey, 30 Euro profit per jersey; Champions League bonus: 40M Euro for winning, 5% incremental probability; TV broadcast bonuses: 3M Euro per year additional

framework: Approach 1 - Benchmarking: compare transfer fee to recent deals for players of similar skill and calibre
Approach 2 - Value-based pricing: estimate incremental profit Real Madrid earns from Wayne Rooney over the contract term, net of his salary, then discount for risks
Synthesise both approaches and recommend a bid range, accounting for negotiating dynamics (Manchester United not selling below fair value; multiple competing clubs)

questions.prompt: Benchmarking approach: What does the comparable-transaction data suggest about a fair transfer fee?
questions.guidance: Candidate should observe that Kaka (65M), Schewtschenko (46M), and Ronaldo (45M) bracket a range of roughly 45-65M Euro for world-class players. Wayne Rooney is widely considered the best English player and compares favourably to Kaka, so a fee at or above the midpoint (~52-65M Euro) is defensible. Candidate should note that multiple bidders and Manchester United's reluctance to sell below fair value support bidding toward the upper end.

math.setup: Range from comparables: 45M - 65M Euro. Midpoint = (45+65)/2 = 55M Euro.
math.answer: Benchmark range: ~45M - 65M Euro; central estimate ~55M Euro

questions.prompt: Value-based pricing - Jersey Sales: What is the incremental profit from jersey sales?
questions.guidance: Candidate should multiply 100M fans x 3% x 30 Euro profit per jersey. This is a one-time Year 1 effect.

math.setup: 100,000,000 fans x 3% = 3,000,000 jerseys sold; 3,000,000 x 30 Euro = 90M Euro

questions.prompt: Value-based pricing - Champions League bonus: What is the incremental expected profit?
questions.guidance: 5% increased probability x 40M Euro bonus = 2M Euro per year.

math.setup: 5% x 40M Euro = 2M Euro per year over 5-year contract

questions.prompt: Value-based pricing - TV broadcast bonuses: What is the incremental profit?
questions.guidance: 3M Euro per year x 5 years = 15M Euro total.

questions.prompt: Value-based pricing - aggregate incremental profit over the 5-year contract
questions.guidance: Sum Year 1 revenues (jersey one-time + CL + TV) and Years 2-5 revenues (CL + TV only). Year 1 incremental profit = 90 + 2 + 3 = 95M; after Year 1 = 5M/year x 4 years = 20M; total = 115M. The casebook states total = 100M as a rounded figure (using 5M/year x 5 years + 95M simplification). Either derivation is acceptable; the casebook's stated answer is 100M.

math.setup: Year 1: 90 (jersey) + 2 (CL) + 3 (TV) = 95M. Years 2-5: (2+3) x 4 = 20M. Total = 115M. Casebook rounds to 100M.
math.answer: ~100M Euro gross incremental profit over 5 years (casebook figure)

questions.prompt: Value-based pricing - net of salary: What is Real Madrid's net incremental profit?
questions.guidance: Salary is 8M Euro/year x 5 years = 40M Euro. Net profit = 100M - 40M = 60M Euro (using casebook's 100M figure, discount rate = 0%).

questions.prompt: Synthesise: What should Real Madrid bid?
questions.guidance: The value-based ceiling is ~60M Euro net profit, meaning a bid above 60M destroys value. The benchmarking range is ~45-65M Euro. A strong candidate reconciles the two: bid up to ~60M Euro, consistent with both fair market value and the value-based ceiling. Given competing interest, Real Madrid should be willing to bid toward the upper benchmark range (55-65M) but not exceed the value-based cap of ~60M. Candidate should note that Real Madrid's president's willingness to pay any price is a negotiating dynamic, not a valuation rationale.

brainstorming.prompt: What risks should Real Madrid discount against the expected 60M Euro net profit when deciding the final bid?

categories.name: Player Performance Risks
ideas: Injuries reducing or eliminating Rooney's contribution during the 5-year contract
Worse-than-expected performance due to adapting to a new team, league, or tactical system
Declining form as Rooney ages over the contract period

categories.name: Commercial / Revenue Risks
ideas: Jersey sales may be lower than 3% if Real Madrid fans are less receptive to an English player
TV bonus uplift may be lower if Rooney does not attract the assumed additional broadcast deals
Champions League win probability uplift may be optimistic

categories.name: Cultural / Market Risks
ideas: Local Manchester fans more receptive to Rooney as an English player; Real Madrid fans may not identify with him as strongly
Language and cultural integration challenges in Spain
Competing clubs may outbid Real Madrid, pushing the transfer cost above the value-based ceiling

recommendation: Real Madrid should bid approximately 55-60M Euro for Wayne Rooney.

The value-based analysis caps the economically rational bid at ~60M Euro net incremental profit over 5 years (at 0% discount rate). The benchmarking analysis shows comparable world-class players traded at 45-65M, consistent with this range.
risks: Injuries or underperformance could significantly reduce the 60M Euro estimated benefit.
Real Madrid fans may be less receptive to Rooney than assumed, reducing jersey revenue.
Multiple competing bidders could push the price above the value-based ceiling; Real Madrid should set a hard cap at ~60M.
next_steps: Conduct deeper due diligence on Rooney's current fitness and injury history.
Refine the jersey sales estimate with fan survey data in the Spanish market.
Monitor competing bids and engage quickly given Manchester United's potential cash pressure.
